references.text: Moses previously asked to find favor in the Lord's eyes, and here the Lord confirms that Moses has found favor (חֵן בְּעֵינַי)
Moses refers to finding favor in the Lord's eyes as the basis for his prayer, which the Lord now answers
Noah found favor in the Lord's eyes (מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה), the same expression used about Moses
The Lord called Moses by name from the burning bush, showing that God knew him personally (וָאֵדָעֲךָ בְּשֵׁם)
The Lord who calls by name and knows His people personally, parallel to God knowing Moses by name
God calls Cyrus by name and gives him a title of honor, showing God's personal knowledge of His chosen ones
The Lord's unique relationship with Moses is confirmed: He speaks with him face to face, not in riddles
No prophet has arisen in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face
The good shepherd calls his sheep by name (κατʼ ὄνομα), parallel to God knowing Moses by name
The Lord knows those who are His (ἔγνω κύριος τοὺς ὄντας αὐτοῦ), God's personal knowledge of His people
Parallel between God revealing His own name ('I AM') and His knowledge of Moses' name.
Direct theological connection: Paul quoted the context from Exodus 33 to explain God's sovereign mercy.
Contrast between human 'favor in the eyes' (Laban) and divine 'favor in the eyes' (God toward Moses).
